newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African stocks raced to their third succesive rise on Friday as major world stock markets surged upward ahead of the festive season, dealers said.
A second biggest ever points rise on Wall Street on Thursday was followed by a strong showing in London and South African shares shook off a start of the week hangover to join in the party.
"It is looking very firm on the back of Wall Street's rise," one dealer said.
There were also local factors adding to the seasonal cheer as share watchers took heart from a firming rand and Thursday's better-than-expected inflation figures.
The all-share index closed up 72.4 points to 6,540.4 as industrials jumped 71.1 points to end at 7,795.8.
Dealers said there had been little futures-related manipulation of the market and a solid level of institutional bargain hunting.
Most blue-chips gained as SA Breweries continued a recent recovery to finish at 115 rand, up 250 cents, and Anglos put on 375 cents to 244 rand.

Encouraging statements from Russia supporting a trade deal with De Beers buoyed the diamond giant's shares in strong volumes. Having touched a day's high of 131 rand, De Beers closed at 130.00 rand, up 150 cents.

It has been an unusually busy week for the market given the approach of the holiday period. A massive futures-related sell-off on Tuesday was followed by a firm rally for the rest of the week, but dealers said things were finally calming down.
"It looks like the holiday season has finally arrived," one dealer said, pointing out volumes were healthy but below previous days.
Gold shares were buoyed by a firmer bullion price in European markets and the gold index put on a tentative 10.6 points to 1,501.9.
However, dealers said as long as bullion traded below $370 there would be little real interest in the shares.

The futures market posted a healthy day with the all-share March contrcat ticking up to 6,085/100 from 5,983 and the industrials contract at 7,685/700 from 7,574. The gold contract attracted less interest but edged up to 1,058/65 from 1,058.
